newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Randstad 1996 profit seen up 24 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Randstad 1996 profit seen up 24 pct.

text.p: Profits of Dutch temporary employment agency Randstad are seen rising 24 percent to around 203 million guilders in 1996, against a 22.5 percent rise in the first half, analysts said.
Randstad is to release its provisional results over 1996 on Monday, January 13 before bourse opening.
When publishing results of the first half of 1996 in September, Randstad said it expected full year profit and turnover to be in line with the first half.
In 1995, Randstad's net profits surged 45 percent to 163.3 million guilders.
Some analysts, however, do not consider the slowdown in profit growth a problem, as they say the company is busy positioning itself for solid future growth.

"Randstad is a very profitable company, which enables them to set up new (initially loss-making) offices, thus enlarging marketshare and promising a continuous growth," said Manus Fleskens, an analyst at BZW.
NIB Strating's Rene Verhoef agreed, saying: "Profit growth will lag somewhat behind the increase in turnover, but the main point is the big investments Randstad has made in its future growth."

"The number of personnel has increased by some 22 percent in 1996, nine percent more offices were opened. For the moment this has pressured margins, as the average of temps sent out per Randstad employee per day will fall to 20 from 23.3 in 1995, but we'll see a positive effect starting 1997."
Randstad's performance in Europe is likely to vary depending on the state of the different markets, the analysts said.
Jurgen Veenker, analyst at MeesPierson, said: "The Netherlands are good, Belgium reasonably satisfactory, France weak and Germany -- still very underdeveloped on the field -- has enormous potential."

Overseas, he said Randstad had had the opportunity to build a name in the U.S. with the Atlanta games, but said the market there was weakening somewhat now, although he saw good long term prospects if it picked up again.
NIB Strating's Verhoef saw the immediate prospects in the U.S. as more favourable.
"In the U.S., I expect a doubling of turnover (for 1996). Although growth seems to slow down in some regions over there, Randstad does not suffer from this as the Atlanta region continues growing."
"During the first half of 1996, Randstad was in the red in the U.S., but the company should be back into the black in the second half."

With a total turnover of 4.7 billion guilders in 1995, Randstad was the Netherland's biggest and Europe's second largest temp agency until ousted from this position by Vendex's announcement of the acquisition of French BIS last Monday.
